promotedEnvironment.label: UAT
promotedEnvironment.remoteUrlTemplate: https://api.uat.hushh.ai/mcp/ (send 'Authorization: Bearer <developer-token>' as a request header — query-string tokens are rejected)

hostExamples.title: Generic mcpServers JSON
hostExamples.whenToUse: your host supports HTTP MCP directly.
hostExamples.secretNote: The API requires 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' — query-string tokens are rejected. Keep the token machine-local and never commit host config with inline credentials.

hostExamples.title: Codex remote setup
hostExamples.whenToUse: Codex should connect to the hosted UAT MCP endpoint directly.
hostExamples.secretNote: Codex's CLI add flow does not take a header flag yet, so add the bearer token to ~/.codex/config.toml under the new [mcp_servers.hushh_consent] table after running this command.
hostExamples.template:
codex mcp add hushh_consent --url "{{API_ORIGIN}}/mcp/"

# Then edit ~/.codex/config.toml and add under [mcp_servers.hushh_consent]:
# bearer_token_env_var = "{{TOKEN_ENV_VAR}}"

hostExamples.title: Codex npm bridge
hostExamples.whenToUse: Codex should launch a local stdio MCP bridge instead of remote HTTP MCP.
hostExamples.secretNote: Keep {{TOKEN_ENV_VAR}} local. The backend endpoint and token should not be committed.

hostExamples.title: npm bridge config
hostExamples.whenToUse: your host expects a local stdio process but supports generic mcpServers JSON.
hostExamples.secretNote: Keep {{TOKEN_ENV_VAR}} local. This should match the same endpoint and token you use for remote MCP.

hostExamples.title: Claude Desktop stdio
hostExamples.whenToUse: Claude Desktop is your MCP host and you need a local stdio bridge.
hostExamples.secretNote: Claude Desktop stores this config locally. Do not commit the token value.

hostExamples.title: Cursor / VS Code remote JSON
hostExamples.whenToUse: your editor host understands mcp.json and can call remote MCP directly.
hostExamples.secretNote: VS Code's HTTP server type accepts a 'headers' map alongside 'url'. Keep the token machine-local; the API rejects query-string tokens.

hostExamples.title: Raw remote MCP URL
hostExamples.whenToUse: your host only asks for the MCP endpoint URL and lets you set a custom header separately.
hostExamples.secretNote: Use the exact slash-safe mount shape and attach 'Authorization: Bearer <developer-token>' as a request header, not a query parameter.
